chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abī Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام would place the liability for the offense of the mentally impaired person upon his ʿāqilah, whether it was accidental or intentional.

key_terms.اَلْمَعْتُوهِ: the mentally impaired or intellectually disabled person
key_terms.جِنَايَةَ: an offense or injurious act that incurs legal liability
key_terms.عَاقِلَتِهِ: his male paternal relatives or legally responsible kin who bear blood-money liability

ai.seo_question: Who bears liability for the offense of a mentally impaired person in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding liability for the offense of a mentally impaired person. It states that the financial responsibility is borne by his ʿāqilah, whether the act occurred by mistake or intentionally, reflecting a jurisprudential principle in bodily injury law.
